title: Before-count subtraction left no clear outer-share rise after 171 shallow M7–8 earthquakes in 2001–2024
abstract: We tested spatial change after 171 isolated shallow centers of preferred magnitude 7 to below 8 in 2001–2024, using a fixed global ComCat M5.5+ snapshot. The share of nearby events above 100 to 300 km rose from 10.6% on days 1–7 to 27.4% on days 7–30. The raw rise was 16.8 percentage points, with a conditional 95% three-year block interval of 10.0 to 26.2 points. After matching before counts were subtracted by radial and time cell, the rise was 3.8 points, with an interval of −12.1 to 19.0. Radial split, magnitude floor and dependence checks also gave subtracted intervals that included zero. Without center isolation, the late excess was negative and its share was undefined. A changing mixture of concentrated activity and background is consistent with the primary result. This does not establish fixed excess spread or physical outward migration. Sparse outer excess counts, selection, mixed magnitudes and the before-background assumption limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and independent count checks are included. Event records remain external.
